name: bully/dot_path

ref_bug.desc: char parameter '\' is emitted as '\' in gas syntax, which gas reads as an escaped quote (0x27 instead of 0x5C)
escape '\v' is emitted as gas '\v', which gas does not know (assembles as 'v' = 0x76 instead of 0x0B)
division: cqo sign-extends the old rax instead of the dividend, so the result is wrong when their signs differ
a function named '$' is emitted as 'call $' which gas reads as 'call <current address>' (endless recursion, SIGSEGV)
x UNLIMITED POWER 1 decrements the exponent twice before testing it and loops ~2^64 times
negative exponent loops ~2^64 times (no defined result)
decimal literal larger than 2^64 is silently saturated to INT64_MAX by strtoll
it's over 9000 with an 8-bit register emits 'cmp al, 9000'; gas truncates 9000 to 0x28 (warning hidden by -w), so al=41 passes the check

name: bugs/bully_operand_size

ref_bug.desc: bully mode operand-size check uses paramTypes[index + 1 % 2] (= index+1), so a pointer in the 2nd parameter gets no size prefix and gas fails with 'ambiguous operand size'

note: the operand size is the bully's choice (Rust: BYTE PTR), so only successful assembly is required

ref_bug.desc: bully mode with no functions at all: the generated main falls through into writechar and returns an uninitialised rax (undefined behaviour)
multi-line comments ('Why, why?' ... "Oh, that's why") are defined in commands.h but never implemented
-O-2 and -O-s share enum value -2 (o_s is not given an explicit value), so -O-2 also emits '.align 536870912' (~1.6 GB executable)
-O-s shares the enum value of -O-2, so it also inserts push rax/pop rax after every command
Windows: writechar zeroes the saved r9 (5th WriteFile argument stored at [rsp+32] after 'sub rsp, 32') and does not preserve r10/r11; prints must not modify registers (Linux prints 'xABCDEF')
bully mode, no main, Windows: the injected main contains the martyrdom code referencing killParent/.LsigStruct (never emitted on Windows), so linking always fails

name: bugs/pb_empty_file

ref_bug.desc: perfectly balanced with several input files, one of them empty (bully mode): rand() % 0 on the empty file, the compiler crashes (SIGSEGV on aarch64, SIGFPE on x86-64)

note: perfectly balanced may delete the function header; then linking fails legitimately, so only 'the compiler terminates normally' is required

ref_bug.desc: bully mode, perfectly balanced when bully fixes already dropped more lines than remain: the deletion loop never ends (compiler hangs)

bully mode, non-mov 64-bit arithmetic with a decimal that does not fit a sign-extended imm32: the string is cut at computedIndex % 32 (out-of-bounds write when shorter) and gas rejects the too large immediate
